overview: Poly Property Services is a leading comprehensive property management company in China, ranked second among the China Index Academy's Top 100 Property Management Companies in 2025/2026 and first among state-owned peers, with a central state-owned enterprise (SOE) background as part of China Poly Group. As at 30 June 2026 it managed approximately 893.7 million sq.m. of gross floor area (GFA) across residential, commercial/office and public property types in 186 cities across 31 provinces, with 1,018.4 million sq.m. of contracted GFA. The group is majority-dependent on its controlling shareholder and sister company, Poly Developments and Holdings Group (600048.SS, China's top-ranked developer by contracted sales), for a large share of its managed GFA, while growing a third-party (non-Poly) management business that now exceeds 65% of GFA under management.

business_model.summary: Poly Property earns recurring, largely fee-based revenue from managing residential, commercial/office and public properties (property management services, ~80% of revenue and growing), supplemented by one-off/project-based value-added services sold to property developers (pre-delivery services, office leasing - mainly to Poly Group, ~8% of revenue and shrinking with the real estate downturn) and recurring community value-added services sold to residents/owners (retail, housekeeping, parking, home furnishing, brokerage - ~12% of revenue, higher margin at ~40-47% gross margin vs ~14-16% for core property management). Revenue is split roughly 55%/45% between GFA developed by parent Poly Developments and third-party developers, with third-party GFA now the larger and faster-growing share (66% of total GFA under management as of mid-2026).
business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2B (property developers, enterprises, government/public institutions) and B2C (residential property owners); property management services contracts are typically long-duration/recurring, value-added services are more transactional/project-based
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% Mainland China operations; concentrated in 50 core cities (contributing ~80% of property management revenue); revenue and costs are RMB-denominated with minimal FX exposure (company holds no borrowings as of FY2025/H1-2026 and reports no significant FX risk)

main_competitors: CTG Duty Free-affiliated/other central-SOE property managers
competitive_position.market_position: Ranked #2 overall among China's Top 100 property management companies (2025/2026, China Index Academy) and #1 among state-owned enterprise property managers; improved from #4 in 2019, reflecting steady scale growth even as the broader real estate sector has contracted

moat_factors.description: Central SOE status under China Poly Group lends credibility with government and institutional clients (public properties, scenic areas, bank headquarters, SOE offices) and supports access to large-scale/public-sector contracts that private peers cannot easily win

Poly Developments remains China's top-ranked developer by contracted sales (RMB253bn in 2025), providing a steady, high-quality stream of new-build management contracts even as its growth has slowed and contracted sales have declined in 2026

Brand valued at ~RMB29.5 billion (2025, China Index Academy) with multiple product sub-brands (Oriental Courtesy, Elegant Life, Harmony Courtyard, Nebula Ecology, Poly Public Services); long track record of national awards for service quality and civic contribution
893.7 million sq.m. under management in 2026 across 186+ cities enables regional cluster management, centralised procurement and supply-chain integration that smaller managers cannot match

Property management contracts can be re-tendered by owners' committees; switching costs are lower than in many B2B models, though incumbency, owner satisfaction and SOE trust provide some renewal advantage

weaknesses: Still partially reliant on related-party developer (Poly Developments) for GFA pipeline and historically for a majority of revenue, exposing the company to the parent's slowing sales and profit decline
Core property management gross margin is thin (~13-16%) and under continued pressure from rising labour/service costs and competitive pricing
Developer-facing value-added services (pre-delivery, office leasing) have declined double digits for multiple consecutive periods as China's real estate development cycle contracts
Receivables growth (trade and bills receivables up from RMB2.8bn to RMB4.4bn between FY2024 and H1-2026) outpacing revenue growth, raising working-capital and collection-risk concerns industry-wide
Community value-added services revenue has also declined in recent periods amid weaker consumer spending

growth_drivers: Continued third-party (non-Poly) market expansion - new third-party contract value has remained in the industry's top tier (RMB2.93bn in FY2025, RMB1.4bn in H1-2026), diversifying away from parent-developer dependency

Expansion into non-residential property types - commercial/office buildings (via 'Nebula Ecology' brand, serving bank headquarters, JD Group, XPeng, SMIC, Goertek) and public/other properties (via 'Poly Public Services' and the new 'Comprehensive Scene-City Model' for urban scenic areas, e.g. Shenzhen Xichong Coastal Tourism Resort)

Shift toward higher-margin 'comprehensive property' and value-added services - IFM (Integrated Facility Management), asset operations, engineering services (energy retrofits, in-home repairs), and cultural-tourism/scenic-area operations intended to build a 'second growth curve'
Steadily rising average property management fee per unit (RMB2.52/sq.m./month in H1-2026 vs RMB2.47 a year earlier) from higher-quality new projects and repricing of existing contracts

Technology/AI-driven efficiency gains - robotics (cleaning robots piloted in 100+ projects), AI-powered video inspection and customer service, and a data middle platform aimed at reducing labour intensity and improving margins

Industry consolidation - management expects scale and brand credibility (especially SOE status) to be increasingly decisive as the industry shifts from a 'scale race' to 'quality competition', favouring leading players like Poly Property
Large net cash balance (~RMB12.9bn cash, no borrowings as of FY2025) provides capacity for selective M&A/strategic investment (per use-of-IPO-proceeds plan) without balance-sheet risk

business.description: Approximately 53-55% of property management revenue still derives from projects developed by Poly Developments and Holdings Group; a slowdown in the parent's new project launches or financial distress would constrain Poly Property's organic GFA pipeline, even though third-party share is rising

Pre-delivery services and office leasing revenue (value-added services to non-property owners) fell ~16-17% YoY in both FY2025 and H1-2026 as China's property development cycle contracts, with no clear bottom yet visible

business.risk: Thin and pressured gross margins in core business
business.description: Property management services gross margin fell from 14.33% (FY2024) to 13.39% (FY2025) and 15.82%->lower in H1-2026 comparisons, reflecting rising labour costs and competitive repricing pressure in a mature, increasingly commoditised segment

Management itself describes an industry shift from 'scale race' to 'quality competition' amid accelerating market differentiation; smaller/weaker players may undercut on price while larger SOE and private peers (China Resources Mixc, Greentown, Onewo) compete for the same high-quality third-party contracts

Two general manager changes within roughly seven months (Yao Yucheng appointed June 2025, resigned January 2026; Wang Yingnan appointed January/March 2026) could signal execution/strategy transition risk, though SOE leadership rotation is relatively common

financial.description: Trade and bills receivables grew from RMB2.8bn (FY2024) to RMB3.4bn (FY2025) to RMB4.4bn (H1-2026), growing faster than revenue, which could signal slower collections from financially stressed developers/owners or weaker owner-fee payment discipline amid the broader property downturn

financial.risk: No committed credit facility disclosed / reliance on operating cash
financial.description: The company carries no borrowings and no pledged assets (strong balance sheet), but this also means limited disclosed external financing cushion if receivables or working capital needs were to spike

regulatory.description: Chinese local governments periodically regulate residential property management fees and owner-committee bidding processes, which can cap pricing power, especially in lower-tier or politically sensitive markets

As a central SOE subsidiary, strategic and capital-allocation decisions may be influenced by state policy objectives (e.g., 'good houses', urban governance initiatives) rather than purely shareholder-return optimization

macro.description: China's new-home sales value is projected to fall another 7-8% in 2026 with no clear bottom (per Fitch), directly curtailing new GFA pipeline from developers (including parent Poly Developments, whose February 2026 contracted sales fell ~37% YoY and FY2025 net profit fell ~84.5%) and pressuring developer-facing value-added services
Community value-added services (retail, housekeeping, home furnishing, brokerage) revenue declined ~14% YoY in H1-2026 amid soft Chinese consumer demand and a weak secondary housing/rental market

macro.risk: Broader China macro slowdown / local government fiscal stress
macro.description: Public-sector and government-facility management contracts (a growth area for Poly Property) could be affected by local government fiscal constraints limiting new public infrastructure/service spending

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's property management industry generated an estimated RMB1.7 trillion in revenue (Fifth National Economic Census), with structural growth drivers (expanding scope from residential to enterprise/government clients, rising service-quality standards under the '15th Five-Year Plan') offsetting cyclical weakness from the real estate downturn; industry consolidation is increasing as weaker, highly-levered or private developer-affiliated managers lose market share to well-capitalised SOE-backed and scale players
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - property management fee revenue is relatively recurring/defensive (acts like an annuity on existing GFA), but new contract wins, value-added services and community services exhibit more cyclicality tied to the broader real estate development and consumer spending cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (no interest-bearing debt as of FY2025/H1-2026); indirect sensitivity via its effect on the broader Chinese property market and developer financing conditions, which influence new contract pipeline
key_input_costs: Labour (frontline property staff - largest cost component)

recent_developments.event: Revenue grew 5.2% YoY to RMB8,829.2 million; profit for the period rose 4.3% YoY to RMB942.7 million; property management services revenue grew 11.9% but value-added services to non-property owners fell 16.7% and community value-added services fell 14.4%

Wang Yingnan appointed general manager (13 March 2026) and executive director, succeeding Yao Yucheng, who resigned as general manager/director on 27 January 2026 after only around seven months in the role
Parent Poly Developments and Holdings Group reported February 2026 contracted sales down approximately 37% YoY, consistent with a sector-wide downturn in new home sales

Full-year revenue grew 4.8% YoY to RMB17,126.1 million and profit grew 5.3% to RMB1,567.9 million; administrative expenses fell 11.5% YoY on regional-cluster management efficiency gains; gearing ratio held flat at 41.2% with zero borrowings and no pledged assets

Completed conversion of 193.7 million domestic shares into H Shares (H Share Full Circulation), listed 15 April 2025, bringing total H Shares to 347.0 million of 553.3 million total issued shares - improving free float and liquidity

Poly Developments and Holdings Group (parent) reported FY2025 revenue of RMB308.1 billion (down 1.1%) but net profit attributable to shareholders down approximately 84.5% YoY, underscoring severe margin/impairment pressure at the controlling shareholder despite Poly Property's own resilient results

UBS downgraded the stock to Neutral/Hold with a HK$36.50 price target (from Buy), while other brokers (CLSA, JPMorgan) maintained Buy ratings with targets in the HK$37-54 range, reflecting a mixed but still broadly constructive analyst view

items.notes: Poly Property does not issue formal numerical revenue/profit/margin guidance in its interim or annual reports; management instead provides qualitative 'Future Development' commentary on strategic priorities

items.target: Build quality foundations, strengthen specialised development ('second growth curve' in home services/asset operations/engineering), safeguard cash flow via lean management, and leverage technology/AI for efficiency
items.notes: Management reiterated the strategic repositioning to 'Premier Operator for Holistic Urban Governance' (upgraded from 'Comprehensive Property' strategy) first articulated in the FY2025 annual report, continued into the H1-2026 interim report without material change

items.target: Continue 'three ploughing' strategy - 50 core cities, high-quality industry clients, core quality business types
items.notes: No specific GFA or contract-value targets disclosed for FY2026, but management flagged continued emphasis on quality/profitability/cash flow over pure scale in third-party expansion

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Wu Lanyu and management MD&A emphasize 'prudent operations and a long-term-oriented perspective' to navigate the real estate downturn, citing the industry's shift from 'scale race' to 'quality competition' and positioning Poly Property to benefit from its SOE brand credibility and balance-sheet strength (zero debt, ~RMB12-13bn cash) as weaker/private competitors struggle. No specific FY2026 revenue, margin or profit targets were disclosed as of the H1-2026 interim report.

bull_case: Central SOE backing and #2 industry ranking provide a durable brand/trust advantage in winning large public-sector, financial-institution and enterprise contracts that private-sector competitors cannot easily match

Debt-free balance sheet with ~RMB12-13 billion in cash provides resilience and optionality for selective M&A/investment while weaker, more leveraged competitors (including some private developer-affiliated managers) are under financial stress

Successful diversification away from parent-developer dependency - third-party GFA now ~66% of total GFA under management (up from well below 60% a few years ago) and growing faster than Poly-sourced GFA, reducing concentration risk over time

Steady core revenue and profit growth (mid-single-digit) has persisted through the broader China property downturn, evidencing the recurring/defensive nature of the core property management fee business

Multiple margin-accretive growth avenues (scenic-area/cultural-tourism operations, IFM for enterprise clients, AI/robotics-driven cost efficiency) offer a credible path to improving blended margins over time
bear_case: Still meaningfully exposed to parent Poly Developments and Holdings Group, whose new-home sales and profitability have deteriorated sharply (FY2025 net profit down ~84.5%; February 2026 contracted sales down ~37% YoY), threatening the pipeline of new Poly-sourced management contracts

China's broader property sector has no clear bottom in sight (new-home sales value projected down another 7-8% in 2026), continuing to pressure developer-facing value-added services (pre-delivery, office leasing) which have now declined double-digits for multiple consecutive periods
Core property management gross margins are thin (13-16%) and have been compressing, with limited visible pricing power against rising labour costs in a maturing, increasingly commoditised segment

Rising trade receivables (up roughly 55% from FY2024 to H1-2026) outpacing revenue growth raises questions about collection discipline and working-capital quality amid a financially stressed property ecosystem
Recent management turnover (two general manager changes within about seven months) introduces near-term execution and strategic-continuity uncertainty
As an H-share SOE-affiliated name, valuation and investor sentiment remain linked to broader China property/SOE risk perception, which can suppress multiples regardless of company-specific execution
